threads.summary: DaveMoreau opened this to flag JSON Object Format requirements that use several [*] paths, or pair a [*] subject with a quantifier, without saying whether the paths refer to the same array element. The guidelines do not settle repeated wildcards, and RFC 9535 would allow either reading. Cases fall into three groups: same element meant but unstated (contractapplied, allocatedmethoddetails); different elements meant, with scope to confirm for the ContractCommitmentId pairing, possibly tied to #2701; and a 'one' versus every-element quantifier mismatch. The proposed fix is an explicit qualifier in each requirement. Matt-Cowsert notes #2827 has dropped its qualifier, leaving Requester Details unqualified, and asks for those lines in the same-element table. No other replies yet, so support looks limited to the author and that commenter. The issue is open with no decision recorded.

threads.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue because the feature request triage guideline assumes every request concerns FOCUS data. Twelve open requests serve people who write and maintain the specification, so their use cases are about spec mechanics, and Gates 2 and 3 have no bar for them. Triagers currently decide case by case. The proposal adds a bar to the guideline covering whose view the problem statement takes, what the use case is about, whose outcome each success criterion states, and what each criterion is checked against, such as the source files or the build. Some of this work may instead suit a Maintenance task, since those cover process rather than spec contents. The change applies to 1.6 only if approved by 28 January 2027, otherwise 1.7. No one has commented yet, so there is no sign of support or objection.

gists.o2824: Matt-Cowsert argued the guideline assumes every request is about FOCUS data, leaving twelve requests serving spec contributors without a Gate 2 or 3 bar, and proposed a separate bar.

threads.summary: This is a wording erratum for the Requester Details object requirements. The rules refer to array items as Entry, a term the specification never defines. The proposal swaps each one for a path starting at RequesterDetailsObject, matching other JSON Object Format columns, with no change to data shape or constraints. The main gain is for the requirements model: with paths, the PrincipalId and CredentialId checks could be Static, so a validator needs only the dataset. Matt-Cowsert opened it on 4 November 2026 after a reviewer raised it on #2802. The array shape and lowercase key and value names are excluded, since they change structure; #2717 tracks the shape. It belongs to the 1.5 errata bundle. No replies yet, so how the group feels is unclear.

gists.o2821: Matt-Cowsert proposed replacing undefined Entry references with RequesterDetailsObject paths, matching other columns and letting validation rules be Static, with no change to data shape.

threads.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 3 November 2026 because the Version Introduced and Version Updated sections have no agreed meaning. Version Introduced shows 0.5 or 1.0-preview on 49 sections, though those were beta releases, and the same column often carries different values across datasets. Version Updated appears on only four supported features, with no rule for which changes count. If it goes ahead, practitioners could see which FOCUS version added or materially changed a column or feature. The FinOps Foundation rates it nice to have, and it came out of the October Maintainers and Task Force 2 meetings. It is tied to held draft PRs #2776 and #2780, both waiting for 1.6. The thread has no replies yet, so reaction is not visible.
